title: "Learning without a backward pass"

Notes on @hinton2022forward.

## Forward-Forward

Layer input $x$ (previous layer's activities), normalized by length only:

$$
\hat x = \frac{x}{\lVert x \rVert}, \qquad y = \mathrm{ReLU}(W \hat x)
$$

Goodness, and probability that the input is positive (real) data:

$$
G = \sum_j y_j^2, \qquad p = \sigma(G - \theta)
$$

Local loss:

$$
\mathcal{L} =
\begin{cases}
-\log p & \text{(positive)}\\
-\log(1 - p) & \text{(negative)}
\end{cases}
$$

Update, using $\partial G / \partial W = 2\, y\, \hat x^{\top}$:

$$
\Delta W =
\begin{cases}
+2\eta\,(1-p)\; y\, \hat x^{\top} & \text{(positive)}\\
-2\eta\, p\; y\, \hat x^{\top} & \text{(negative)}
\end{cases}
$$

Inputs to the update: $\hat x$, $y$, $p$, all local to the layer.

Negative data:

- supervised: one-hot label in the first 10 pixels; correct label = positive, wrong label = negative
- unsupervised: $m \odot x_1 + (1 - m) \odot x_2$, with $m$ a random bit image blurred by $[\tfrac14, \tfrac12, \tfrac14]$ and thresholded at 0.5

Classification (supervised), one pass per label $c$:

$$
\hat c = \arg\max_c \sum_{\ell \ge 2} G_\ell(x, c)
$$

## Backprop

$$
\delta_\ell = \big(W_{\ell+1}^{\top}\, \delta_{\ell+1}\big) \odot f'(a_\ell), \qquad \Delta W_\ell = -\eta\, \delta_\ell\, h_{\ell-1}^{\top}
$$

Inputs to the update: $W_{\ell+1}, \dots, W_L$, $f'$ at every layer from $\ell$ up, stored $a_\ell$ and $h_{\ell-1}$.

Physical layers $h_{\ell+1} = f_\ell(h_\ell; \theta_\ell)$:

$$
\nabla_{\theta_\ell} L = J_{\theta_\ell}^{\top}\, J_{\ell+1}^{\top} \cdots J_{L}^{\top}\, \nabla_{h_{L+1}} L,
\qquad J_k = \frac{\partial f_k}{\partial h_k}, \quad J_{\theta_\ell} = \frac{\partial f_\ell}{\partial \theta_\ell}
$$

Each $J_k$ is a derivative of the physical device at its operating point.

## Cost per example, digital

$F$ = arithmetic of one forward pass, $L$ = number of layers.

| | arithmetic | activations held |
|---|---|---|
| backprop | $3F$ | $L$ layers |
| backprop + checkpointing [@chen2016training] | $\approx 4F$ | $O(\sqrt{L})$ layers |
| FF | $4F$ ($5F$ with hard-negative mining) | 1 layer |

MNIST [@hinton2022forward, §3]: backprop ≈ 20 epochs, FF 60 epochs, so FF ≈ 4–5× the arithmetic.

45 nm energies [@horowitz2014computing]: FP32 multiply 3.7 pJ, FP32 add 0.9 pJ, DRAM access 1.3–2.6 nJ.

Activation stash vs. arithmetic for a layer of width $d$, at 640 pJ per 32-bit DRAM access [@han2016eie]:

$$
\frac{E_{\text{stash}}}{E_{\text{arith}}} \approx \frac{2 \times 640\ \text{pJ}}{3d \times 4.6\ \text{pJ}} \approx \frac{93}{d}
$$

Measured, ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, Jetson Orin Nano [@ma2025ffint8]:

| training | energy |
|---|---|
| FP32 backprop | 18,764 J |
| INT8 backprop | 10,291 J |
| INT8 FF (loss not purely local) | 9,926 J |

## Physical hardware

Resistive crossbar [@gokmen2016acceleration]:

- forward: $I_i = \sum_j G_{ij} V_j$
- backward: drive the columns to multiply by $W^{\top}$
- update: $\Delta G_{ij} \propto x_i\, \delta_j$ by pulse coincidence, all devices in parallel

FF update in the same rank-1 form: $\Delta W = s\, y\, \hat x^{\top}$, $s \in \{\, 2\eta(1-p),\ -2\eta p \,\}$.

Optical goodness: $G = \sum_j |E_j|^2 \propto$ total optical power.

Ways to get gradients on physical hardware:

| method | requires |
|---|---|
| physics-aware training [@wright2022deep] | digital model of the device for the backward pass |
| in situ backprop [@hughes2018training; @pai2023experimentally] | reciprocal device, forward + adjoint field measurements, digital nonlinearities |
| weight perturbation [@jabri1992weight] | no model; learning rate $\propto 1/(\text{number of perturbed variables})$ |
| ADCs + digital gradients | ADCs: 58% of tile power in ISAAC [@shafiee2016isaac] |
| equilibrium propagation [@scellier2017equilibrium] | energy-based system; free phase + weakly clamped phase |
| FF | $\hat x$, $y$, $p$ per layer |

Reference points: optical MNIST inference at ≈ 90% accuracy with < 1 detected photon per multiplication [@wang2022optical]; human brain ≈ 20 W [@balasubramanian2021brain].

## Results

Test error, @hinton2022forward §3–4:

| task | backprop | FF |
|---|---|---|
| MNIST, fully connected, permutation-invariant | ≈ 1.4% (≈ 20 epochs) | 1.36% (60 epochs, 4 × 2000 ReLUs) |
| MNIST, unsupervised + linear classifier | — | 1.37% (100 epochs); 1.16% local receptive fields (60 epochs) |
| MNIST, ±2-pixel jitter | ≈ 0.6% (CNN) | 0.64% (500 epochs) |
| CIFAR-10, local receptive fields, 2 / 3 layers | 37% / 39% | 41% / 41% |

Since:

| work | result |
|---|---|
| @oguz2023forward | multimode fiber as a fixed layer, MNIST subset: FF 90.8% → 94.4% accuracy with the fiber; LeNet-5 backprop 95.0% |
| @momeni2023backpropagation | model-free FF-style local learning on acoustic and microwave hardware and a modeled optical system; vowel classification |
| @dooms2024trifecta | CIFAR-10 ≈ 84% (backprop 89%); CIFAR-100 36% (backprop 60%) |

## Claims in the paper

- §1: FF "is unlikely to replace backpropagation for applications where power is not an issue."
- §7: "FF has no problem learning if we insert a black box between layers that are being trained by FF."
- §8: "The use of two forward passes instead of a forward and a backward pass should make these A-to-D converters unnecessary."
- §9: "If you want your trillion parameter neural net to only consume a few watts, mortal computation may be the only option."
